subject.title: Write tool lacks append mode — isolated cron sessions destroy shared files

question: Should OpenClaw accept append as an optional parameter on the existing write tool, or require a separate append tool/API before merging the linked implementation?
rationale: The report is source-reproducible and data-loss-prone, but adding append changes the model-facing file-tool contract and needs maintainer intent before another repair lane should act.

options.title: Accept append: true on write
options.body: Use the linked PR shape if it preserves overwrite defaults, path guards, mutation serialization, sandbox behavior, and focused regression coverage.

options.title: Require a separate append tool
options.body: Ask for a dedicated append primitive with the same path policy and concurrency tests instead of extending write.

options.title: Defer general append
options.body: Keep only the memory-flush wrapper and document backups/workarounds, accepting that ordinary cron and agent writes remain unsafe for append workflows.

recommendation.title: Accept append: true on write
recommendation.body: Use the linked PR shape if it preserves overwrite defaults, path guards, mutation serialization, sandbox behavior, and focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Shakker is the strongest current-main history signal for the write-tool modules where the API decision lands.
